thread:
sre-alex: Heads up — getting intermittent packet loss on the VXLAN overlay in us-west2 affecting GPU inference pods. p99 latency spikes + some gRPC streams drop.

maria: saw the pager. which nodes? any pattern?

luke: net-monitor-bot flagged node-gpu-13 and node-gpu-21 with ~0.6-1.2% drop in last 10m.

net-monitor-bot: ALERT: overlay_pkt_drop > 0.5% on cluster/gpu-us-west2 (nodes: node-gpu-13,node-gpu-21). window=10m severity=warning

maria: can you grab tcpdump on one of the affected nodes? start with node-gpu-13.

sre-alex: running quick capture now: `sudo tcpdump -i vxlan0 -n -s 0 -w /tmp/vxlan-gpu13.pcap`

luke: curious if MTU mismatch or offloads. any kernel/driver changes this week?

sre-alex: we pushed kernel 6.1.12 -> 6.1.20 to a small canary group last night (infra image). affected nodes are in that canary.

maria: that could be it. share tcpdump sample? even a hexdump of failing packets helps.

sre-alex: extracted a few lines from tshark:
```
08:21:14.123456 IP 10.10.5.12.39302 > 10.10.6.33.443: Flags [P.], seq 12345:12580, ack 67890, win 64240, length 235
08:21:14.123509 IP 10.10.6.33.443 > 10.10.5.12.39302: Flags [.], ack 12580, win 65535, length 0
08:21:14.223600 IP 10.10.5.12 > 10.10.6.33: ICMP frag needed and DF set (MTU 1450)
```

luke: ICMP 'frag needed' from the VTEP interface — suggests encap added overhead pushed frames over MTU. what is the vxlan and physical MTU?

sre-alex: on node-gpu-13: `ip link show dev eth0` => mtu 9000; `ip link show dev vxlan0` => mtu 1500 (weird).

maria: aha. host NIC is jumbo but vxlan device mtu is 1500. if anything in path expects 9000 but vxlan lower, fragmentation or drops can happen. did kernel change vxlan default behavior?

infra-bot: recent-image: kernel=6.1.20, openvswitch=2.17.1, mlx5-driver=5.12.3

luke: also check offloads: `ethtool -k eth0` and `ethtool -k vxlan0` — GSO/GRO/TSO interplay can cause weird drops with encap.

sre-alex: ethtool shows on eth0: gso:on gro:on tso:on; vxlan0 inherits gro/gso state? quick test: disabled GRO/GSO on eth0 and watched drop rate.

maria: please paste commands used to repro/remove quickly so we can rollback at node level.

sre-alex: ran: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` on node-gpu-13. drop rate dropped to ~0.05% within 2 minutes.

luke: that points to offload interaction post-kernel bump. maybe kernel changed encapsulation handling or driver behavior for large segments.

maria: temporary mitigation = disable offloads on affected hosts or set vxlan mtu to 9000 to match underlying. but setting vxlan mtu=9000 might expose other switches that don't support jumbo. check underlay.

sre-alex: did quick `ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 9000` — was able to set but not safe cluster-wide. underlay between racks reports 1500 on an intermediate switch (so raising vxlan to 9000 risks blackholing).

luke: long-term we need a driver/kernel patch or consistent MTU across underlay + vxlan. short-term: rollout offload disable as a flag for kernel 6.1.20 nodes. we can add kube daemonset to tweak ethtool settings on boot for nodes in the canary.

maria: create a short-lived DaemonSet that runs `ethtool -K $IF gro off gso off tso off` for eth0 on these nodes and run in parallel with canary. Tag nodes with label `image=6.1.20` and target it.

sre-alex: pushing a quick DS to the canary cluster. patch: `kubectl apply -f fix-offload-ds.yaml` (runs as privileged). Monitoring now.

net-monitor-bot: INFO: applied ds/fix-offload-ds to 12 nodes, ready=12

luke: also file kernel bug with vendor (Mellanox if present) — driver might mishandle GRO/GSO with VXLAN + encap. add pcap and ethtool dumps to the ticket.

maria: good. action items: 1) DS to disable offloads for canary nodes (in progress). 2) Rollback kernel on the most critical nodes if drop rate persists. 3) Engage infra-apps to verify underlay MTU and plan for consistent jumbo frames if we want to keep offloads. 4) Open ticket with NIC vendor + kernel network team.

sre-alex: temporary mitigation looks effective on node-gpu-13 and node-gpu-21 — drop rates fell to <0.1% and downstream inference errors reduced. Will continue monitoring through the hour.

maria: thanks. if we still see issues after DS, start node drain + rolling restart of 6.1.20 nodes. keep alerts muted if we know it's the mitigation so we don't noise pagers.

luke: added follow-up: run `iperf3 -c <peer> -P 8 -t 60` and `sudo tcpdump -i vxlan0 -w /tmp/post-fix.pcap` to validate no reordering/fragmentation.

infra-bot: ticket created: INFRA-3421 "VXLAN packet loss after kernel 6.1.20 — offload interaction" assigned to eng-net. attachments: /artifacts/vxlan-gpu13.pcap, ethtool-dumps.txt

sre-alex: will update INFRA-3421 with measured p99 improvements and DS rollout notes. updating channel if anything regresses. :thumbsup:

maria: great work team. once kernel vendor response in, weigh options: kernel patch vs permanent offload disable vs enforced MTU across fabric. prefer patch but need safe interim at scale.

luke: FYI — this one only affected encapsulated intra-node flows (east-west). North-south to external endpoints looked fine. suggests issue with encap handling in NIC path.

sre-alex: last check at 08:52: drop avg now 0.07% cluster-wide for affected nodes. closing temporary oncall loop but keeping the DS live until INFRA-3421 has a mitigation plan.

net-monitor-bot: RESOLVED? overlay_pkt_drop on cluster/gpu-us-west2 now 0.06% (threshold 0.5%).

maria: saved commands and notes to /runbooks/vxlan-offload-mitigation.md for SRE playbook."
